coach.name: Travis Steele
coach.since: 2022 (5th season at Miami in 2026-27; Dayton Daily News' Nov 1, 2026 story says 'sixth season', which conflicts with the MAC/Wikipedia count of five)
coach.notes: Entered 2026-27 at 84-48 (.636) at Miami, 47-25 (.653) in MAC play, 154-98 (.611) overall including Xavier (2018-22). Win totals at Miami: 12, 15, 25, 32. 2025-26: 32-2, 18-0 MAC, program-record 32 wins, undefeated regular season, MAC regular-season title, lost to UMass in MAC Tournament, at-large NCAA bid, beat SMU in the First Four (first NCAA win since 1999), lost to Tennessee in the Round of 64. Learned under Kelvin Sampson at Indiana and under Sean Miller, Chris Mack and Thad Matta at Xavier. Told ClutchPoints he stayed because 'the job isn't finished yet' and plans to play nine players. No contract/salary details found in coverage read.

previews.title: MAC Announces 2026-27 Men's Basketball Preseason Poll, All-MAC Teams
previews.projected_finish: 1st of 12 (130 points, 9 of 12 first-place votes); 5 of 12 votes to win the MAC Tournament
previews.summary: Miami was the overwhelming preseason favorite, taking nine first-place votes and 130 points ahead of Toledo (117), Akron (110) and Kent State (108). Miami also drew the most votes (5) to win the MAC Tournament, ahead of Toledo (4), UMass (2) and Kent State (1). Senior guard Evan Ipsaro and junior guard Luke Skaljac were both named Preseason All-MAC First Team.

previews.title: Miami RedHawks open as MAC favorites; two guards land preseason honors
previews.author: WKRC staff
previews.summary: Local TV write-up of the coaches' poll. Miami, entering Travis Steele's fifth season, returns 11 players from the 32-win team that went undefeated in the regular season, won the MAC regular-season title and won a First Four game. Ipsaro (Cincinnati native, Covington Catholic) and Skaljac were named Preseason All-MAC First Team; Ipsaro, Skaljac and senior forward Almar Atlason are the three captains. The piece notes Miami is seeking consecutive MAC regular-season titles for the first time since the early 1990s.

Junior guard, captain, Preseason All-MAC First Team.

previews.title: Exclusive: Miami (OH) coach Travis Steele won't stop hunting after historic 32-win season, NCAA Tournament breakthrough
previews.author: Richard Pereira
previews.summary: Interview with Steele ahead of his fifth season. He says Miami will 'always be the hunter, not the hunted' and that 'the job isn't finished yet,' with Elite Eight/Final Four ambitions. He expects to play nine players and cites ball movement, shooting and a bigger back line in man-to-man defense as strengths. Returning captains are Skaljac (took over at point guard when Ipsaro was hurt), Atlason (9.9 PPG off the bench, moving to the four after changing his body) and Ipsaro (recently cleared from injury). Peter Suder (14.8 PPG team leader) is gone, as are Brant Byers (Penn State) and Eian Elmer (Wisconsin). Non-conference has no power-conference opponents (James Madison, Wright State, High Point); MAC play expands from 18 to 22 games.

player_claims.claim: Became starting point guard when Ipsaro was injured mid-season; Steele praised his end-of-season play.

previews.title: Miami men's basketball: Roster set for 2026-27 season
previews.author: Chris Vogt (Contributing Writer)
previews.summary: Spring roster rundown of 16 players entering Steele's fifth year after the 32-2, 18-0 season. Freshmen Alan Horton (6-9; 11.7 pts/9.8 reb as a HS junior), Anthony Fresh (6-4; 20.9 pts as a HS junior) and Danny Kelly (6-5 Moeller; 10.1 pts as a senior) join transfers Preston Copeland (Ball State, 4.6/4.4, 24 starts), Stevie Elam (Milwaukee, 10.5 pts/4.7 reb, 12 starts) and Rich Rolf (Youngstown State, 9.1/4.5/2.1, 30 starts). Returners include Ipsaro (13.9 pts in 12 games, injury), Skaljac (10.3 pts, team-high 149 assists), Kirby (6.2 pts, 52.5% FG), Atlason (9.9 pts, 60 threes at 36.4%), Robbins (3.1 pts, 17 blocks), Kotecki (17 games), Waltz (3.0 pts), Wright, Stowers and senior guard Blake Anderson. At the time, the paper listed Antwone Woolfolk as graduated alongside Peter Suder and Eli Yofan; Woolfolk later returned (Aug 2026). Blake Anderson does not appear on the official 2026-27 roster as of Nov 2026.

storylines.headline: Hunter, not hunted: encore after 32-2 and a First Four win
storylines.detail: Miami is the unanimous-in-spirit favorite (9 of 12 first-place votes) and chasing back-to-back MAC regular-season titles for the first time since the early 1990s, with a target on its back and an expanded 22-game MAC schedule.

storylines.headline: Evan Ipsaro back from a torn ACL
storylines.detail: Ipsaro tore his ACL in late December 2025 (12 games played), was cleared in October, and scored 15 with 5 assists in the Nov 2 opener at JMU, his first game since the injury.

storylines.headline: Antwone Woolfolk's fifth season after a summer of eligibility concerns
storylines.detail: Woolfolk (Rutgers transfer, 9.8 PPG/5.3 RPG, All-MAC HM) was announced as returning for 2026-27 on Aug 7, 2026 per the official site, after what The Miami Student called 'a summer with eligibility concerns'; Caleb's Corner flagged him as a fifth-year player 'attempting to play.' He played and grabbed 10 rebounds at JMU. The Miami Student ran a Sept 2026 column questioning the precedent; details of the waiver were not readable this session.

storylines.headline: Replacing Suder, Byers and Elmer
storylines.detail: MAC POY Peter Suder exhausted eligibility; All-MAC second-teamers Brant Byers (Penn State) and Eian Elmer (Wisconsin) and freshman Trey Perry (Coastal Carolina) left via the portal. Steele replaced them with Stevie Elam (Milwaukee), Rich Rolf (Youngstown State), Preston Copeland (Ball State) and freshmen Horton, Fresh and Kelly.

storylines.headline: Skaljac's emergence at point guard
storylines.detail: Junior Luke Skaljac took over at point guard after Ipsaro's injury, earned All-MAC Third Team, and was named a captain and Preseason All-MAC First Team; he led Miami with 19 points at JMU.
